statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH. Tail 24% sits at the top of the watch band, just below the block threshold, as a global bond rout pushes the US 10-year to 5.14% and NQ futures to the bottom of their overnight range.
recommendation: Tail remains inside the watch band, so the deterministic mapping yields WATCH rather than a blocking state. The evidence-based danger window covers the 12:30-16:00 UTC claims, cash-open and Fed-speaker sequence, where opening-auction continuation or a renewed bond leg would be the first genuine evidence of mean-reversion failure.
headline: Global bond rout pushes yields to multi-decade highs as Nasdaq-100 futures press overnight lows
body: NQ futures trade near 30,484.50, down 0.91%, within roughly five points of the 30,479.00 session low after a steady decline from the 30,813.00 overnight high. The driver is duration rather than equity-specific news: the US 10-year yield has extended to about 5.14%, its highest since July 2007, with the 2-year near 4.91%, while Japan's 10-year jumped roughly 10 basis points to about 3.087%, the highest since August 1996. That global bond rout has sapped risk appetite and weighed on chip and AI-linked names. VIX has risen to 16.07 from a 15.18 close and is pressing its 16.08 session high, and energy is adding to the inflation channel with Brent at $105.94, up 2.77%, and WTI at $94.20 amid uncertainty around US-Iran negotiations. Latest-session breadth context is delayed and non-real-time, but it was negative across all seven tracked semiconductors and mixed across megacaps, with GOOGL down 3.80% and AVGO down 2.62% against gains in META and MSFT. Several independent amplifiers are therefore aligned at once: yields extending to a cycle high, oil extending, implied volatility rising, semiconductors soft and NQ holding near a session extreme. Two things argue against treating this as a pathological path. The total overnight decline is about 1.1% from the high and leaves NQ close to the 30,470.29 Nasdaq-100 cash close, and the prior cash session traded a 30,353.88-30,706.23 range yet closed at 30,470.29, well above its low, so retracement was still being rewarded as recently as yesterday's close. Tail therefore moves up to the top of the watch band rather than across the block threshold, while Stress carries the macro backdrop. The structural checkpoints ahead are the 12:30 UTC jobless claims, the 13:30 UTC cash open, a cluster of Fed speakers through the afternoon, and headline risk from the Trump-Xi summit taking place today.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding hourly slots carry published Claude assessments. Tail ran 12-15% through the European and early US hours of Sep 23 in a normal-to-mixed regime, then stepped to 25% for the 14:00 UTC hour as the post-PMI bond leg developed, the only blocking-band reading in the window. It held 20-24% through the US afternoon and into the Asian session, eased to 17-19% between 01:00 and 03:00 UTC, printed 22% at 04:00 UTC on a brief trend-down read, and finished the window at 21-22% for the 06:00 and 07:00 UTC hours. Stress was the more persistent signal, rising from the mid-30s to a 57% peak at 18:00 UTC and holding around 50% overnight. Confidence stayed in the 84-88% band throughout.
outlookSummary: The published path holds Tail at the top of the watch band through the European morning, then crosses briefly into the block band at 25-26% across the 13:00-15:00 UTC claims, cash-open and Fed-speaker sequence, which is the narrow evidence-based danger window. It eases back to 19-22% through the US afternoon and evening and sits at 19-21% across the Asian and following European hours. Stress follows the same shape at a higher level, peaking at 61%, because the multi-decade-high yield level and the open energy channel persist regardless of intraday structure. Confidence decays from 85% to 78% as the current price-path evidence ages. The forecast assumes the rate-repricing regime stays unresolved but that price discovery remains orderly; observed opening-auction continuation with shallow pullbacks would argue for a higher Tail than published, while a cooling bond market or a genuine two-way cash open would argue for a lower one.
